agencies.lines: Milwaukee County Transit System: CONNECT 1 bus rapid transit (rapid) and the bus routes that run every 15 minutes at the morning peak
Madison Metro: Rapid Route A (rapid) and Routes A, B, C, D and 80, which run at least every 15 minutes on weekdays
Eau Claire Transit: Routes 9 and 19 run every 20 minutes, so they count only in the wider definitions

ladder.label: Rail and rapid transit only, within ½ mile
Main case: rail and rapid transit within ½ mile, plus buses every 15 minutes within ¼ mile
Wider: as the main case, plus buses every 20 minutes within ¼ mile
Rail, rapid transit and 15-minute buses, all within ½ mile
Rail, rapid transit and 20-minute buses, all within ½ mile
Any bus or train stop within ½ mile (for context, not "major" transit)

law.label: Within ¼ mile of a rail or rapid transit station
¼ to ½ mile from a rail or rapid transit station
Within ¼ mile of a stop on a bus route every 15 minutes

reference_line.info: The median of the three studies. It equals the typical response, so it is drawn as a dotted line on top of it.
reference_line.label: Median of the three studies

scenarios.info: Like Los Angeles's Transit Oriented Communities program (2017), the only US transit program with a measured citywide net effect. It added 0.04 percentage points to the city's housing growth over six years, and it required affordable homes, which the modelled law does not.
scenarios.label: Little response
scenarios.source: Los Angeles TOC: 0.04 pp over 6 years x 5/6 / 0.61 coverage; New York pooled ramp

scenarios.evidence: like the average loosening reform in 1,136 US cities
scenarios.info: Like the average zoning reform that loosened rules in a study of 1,136 US cities (Stacy and others, 2023): about +0.8% more addresses three or more years after each reform. Most of those reforms were about accessory dwellings and lot sizes, not transit upzonings.
scenarios.label: Typical response
scenarios.source: Stacy et al. 2023: 0.008 per loosening reform, years 3+ after; applied inside 2027-2031 on the New York pooled ramp (the paper shows no ramp)

scenarios.info: Like Auckland, New Zealand, which upzoned three-quarters of its residential land in 2016 and permitted 21,808 extra homes over 2016–2021, net of building moved from elsewhere in the city.
scenarios.label: Strong response
scenarios.source: Auckland: 21,808 / 530,300 = 4.11% / 0.752 coverage; Auckland 2017-2021 profile rescaled to the stated total

timing_caveat: The studies measured their effects three or more years after each reform. The model places that effect inside 2027–2031, the law's first five years. Much of a real law's effect may come after 2031, so the yearly path is the least certain part of these numbers.
